newsitem.title: UK: Brent Walker says under no immediate threat.
newsitem.headline: Brent Walker says under no immediate threat.

text.p: Heavily indebted British leisure group Brent Walker Plc said Wednesday that a French court ruling ordering it to pay more than three million stg to its founder George Walker does not put it under any immediate threat.
Press reports had suggested that the award of 3.3 million stg plus interest to Walker in respect of a debt claim could force the group's bankers to place the company in receivership.
But a spokesman told Reuters that the group's appeal against the award could take between 18 months and two years to be heard and the sum does not have to be paid within that time.
"A lot can happen in two years," he said.
"If the company had to pay the debt immediately it is doubtful whether the company could afford it, but it hasn't got to pay it," he said.
The spokesman said the award figure of six million pounds quoted in some reports was not an official amount. "We don't know where that has come from," he said.
An announcement of a preferred bidder for the group's Pubmaster pubs chain, which is on the market for around 200 million stg, is likely before Christmas, he added.
Reports had suggested the disposal was in jeopardy.

The result of a dispute between Brent Walker and leisure giant Grand Metropolitan Plc over the price Brent Walker paid for the William Hill betting chain in 1989 is due to be published next Monday, the spokesman said.
Accountants Arthur Andersen are investigating claims by Brent Walker that it paid over the odds for William Hill, and in particular that the unit's 1989 profits were overstated.
Brent Walker paid 685 million stg for William Hill in 1989. It has been up for sale since 1991 with a price tag of around 500 million stg.
